title: Lesson 33 - Modeling Decisions That Decide Unification Quality
description: Model data in Data 360., focused on the modeling decisions that determine unification quality: primary keys, normalization, timestamps and record currency, multi-currency and locale, and how a bad model surfaces as bad segments.

questions.question: After unification, a segment shows duplicate profiles for what should be the same customer. Which modeling decision most likely explains it?
options: Inconsistent Individual ID formatting or keys across sources, so the same person never matched.
Too few fields on the Individual object.
The segment is scheduled at the wrong time.
questions.explanation: Matching depends on a consistently populated, consistently formatted Individual ID; small differences across sources split one person into several profiles. Object counts, field counts, and schedule do not cause duplicate profiles.

questions.question: Which pair of modeling choices most directly protects most-recent-value logic and correct monetary aggregates?
options: Timestamps mapped for freshness, and a currency field stored with amounts.
More custom fields on each object.
Larger data streams with more columns.
questions.explanation: Timestamps let Data 360 choose the freshest value and order events, and a currency alongside the amount keeps aggregates comparable. Layouts and profiles are unrelated, and more fields or columns do not fix currency or freshness problems.

questions.question: Where should format standardization, such as dates, phone numbers, and text casing, ideally happen for a Data 360 model?
options: At or before mapping, during stream field mapping and transformation.
Never, because Data 360 standardizes everything automatically.
Only in each source system's user interface.
questions.explanation: Normalizing at mapping time makes the fix reproducible across every consumer. Doing it per segment is not reproducible, automatic standardization of arbitrary source formats is not something to rely on, and relying on source UIs leaves the model inconsistent.
